marketmatters.podbean.com/15e8e7b4-cac1-.recap: Hannah Elson (JPMorgan Custody/Security Services) and Oli Harris (head of Connexus, JPMorgan's blockchain unit) discuss why tokenization is moving from pilots to production. Harris attributes the shift to three forces: market-structure convergence (assets, participants and cash finally on the same rails), sharper regulatory clarity letting institutions commit capital, and the emergence of a credible on-chain cash leg via regulated tokenized deposits like JPMorgan's own deposit token (JPM Coin), which enables true delivery-versus-payment. Higher rates have made idle liquidity costly, pushing collateral efficiency and settlement timing to board-level concerns. Elson adds that stablecoin growth is fueling demand for tokenized yield products (money-market funds) and that crypto-native fintechs are now serious servicing competitors. Client trends cited: asset managers launching tokenized money-market funds to tap blockchain-based investors and stablecoin reserve flows, exploration of tokenized funds as collateral, tokenized equities/bonds (DTCC, UK digital gilt plans), and treasury clients seeking reduced pre-funding via netting and 24/7 cross-border payments. Connexus reports $4 trillion transacted cumulatively and ~$7 billion/day currently, with atomic FX settlement across eight currencies including Hong Kong dollar and renminbi. Both speakers flag privacy/governance/finality on public chains and poor user experience/integration as the key remaining obstacles, predicting tokenization becomes invisible infrastructure within five years rather than a separate market.
terms: DvP -- delivery versus payment, simultaneous exchange of securities and cash to eliminate settlement risk
